title: Today in one sentence
text: At the close on Tuesday, health stocks led (Eli Lilly rose 3.5%) while GE Aerospace fell 3.7% after its quarterly report, and the next big events are Lockheed Martin's report on Thursday and the Fed meeting on October 27 and 28.

title: GE Aerospace fell after its report
text: GE reported third quarter results today. Its own release shows orders up 49% to $19.0 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $2.25, up 36%, and the company raised its 2026 outlook. Even so, the stock fell 3.7% to $299.87. Prices move on what investors expected, not only on what a company reports.

title: Health stocks led the day
text: Healthcare companies on the Nasdaq rose about 2.0% on average, the best sector. Eli Lilly gained 3.5% and Intuitive Surgical 1.1%. We did not verify a single cause for Lilly's jump, so treat it as one day of data.

title: Big tech slipped, chips mixed
text: Meta fell 1.6%, Alphabet 1.1% and AMD 0.6%, while TSMC rose 1.2%. The Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ ended almost flat, down 0.1%. After Monday's bounce, a quiet or mixed day is normal.

title: Rates stay in focus before the Fed
text: The Federal Reserve meets October 27 and 28. After the Fed chair spoke on October 16, traders put the odds of a hike at that meeting below 15%. The 10 year Treasury yield was near 5.1% last Friday, near its highest levels since 2002.

title: Lesson 15: What is a sector?
text: A sector is a group of companies that do a similar kind of work. Technology, healthcare, energy and banks are all sectors. Think of a school with different clubs: each club is a sector, and the students are the companies. Sectors often move in different directions on the same day. On Tuesday, healthcare stocks rose about 2% while energy and consumer staples fell. Holding companies from several sectors is one way to avoid putting all your eggs in one basket. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell anything.
